answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with one vote per locked token rather than one per account. Splitting funds across a thousand Sybils does not multiply voting weight; the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing if identities collude or misbehave. A mesa, shale, and jetty can serve as labels for test agents, but none grants extra influence: only locked stake counts.
